Dear Principal,

I am writing to share my view on the proposed policy that would require students to earn at least a B average before taking part in sports or other activities. I understand the goal behind this idea. We all want students to succeed in the classroom. However, I believe this policy would do more harm than good, and I hope you will consider the reasons below before making a decision.

First, many students currently have a C average, and this policy would remove them from the activities that often keep them motivated. For many of us, sports and clubs are the reason we come to school at all. Practice gives us a place to belong, a set of goals outside of tests, and adults who notice when we are doing well. If we are cut off from those things, we are more likely to lose interest in school entirely, not less. A student who is struggling in math does not need to be pulled away from the team that gives him a reason to show up each morning.

Second, activities teach skills that grades do not measure. On the field, in the band room, or on the debate team, students learn to manage their time, work with people who are different from them, and recover from losing. These lessons carry into the classroom. Many students who play sports learn to plan their homework around practice, and that discipline often improves their grades over time. Taking away the activity removes the very structure that could help a struggling student improve.

Third, the policy could fall hardest on the students who need support the most. Students with a C average are often not lazy. Some are working jobs to help their families, some are dealing with problems at home, and some simply learn in a different way. Excluding them from activities punishes them for their circumstances without offering any real help. If the goal is better grades, the school should offer tutoring, study halls, or extra teacher time to these students, so they can raise their averages while staying connected to the activities they love.

Finally, a grade requirement could make activities less fair and less safe for everyone. Coaches and advisors would be pushed to focus on eligibility paperwork rather than on teaching and mentoring. Students who lose eligibility mid-season could be pulled from a team just when they most need its support. It would be better to set up a system where students who fall behind receive early warnings, a plan to improve, and help along the way.

For these reasons, I respectfully ask you not to adopt a B average requirement. I believe students should be encouraged to stay in activities, and that the school should invest in helping every student raise their grades. I would be glad to take part in any discussion or student survey that would help us find a better solution.

Thank you for asking for our opinions and for considering this important question.

Respectfully,

A Concerned Student
